### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**9** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **8** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `76f84229cf98a12f14114524e2f15aaa1c08eeeb` — the merge of head `cda55e65473673ae0db2ebae9b3aac7143384404` into base `2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 76f84229cf98a12f14114524e2f15aaa1c08eeeb && git checkout 76f84229cf98a12f14114524e2f15aaa1c08eeeb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af cda55e65473673ae0db2ebae9b3aac7143384404 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af && git merge --no-ff cda55e65473673ae0db2ebae9b3aac7143384404

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cda55e65473673ae0db2ebae9b3aac7143384404`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/wasm-connection.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-driver-durability.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-25019-unreadable-file-refused.test.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/sqlite-driver-fallback.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/sqlite-driver-fallback-wasm-unreadable-file.test.ts + packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-driver.ts (`isSqlite`, `toKnexConfig`, `connect`, `disconnect`), packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/knex-wasm-dialect.ts (`acquireRawConnection`, `destroyRawConnection`), packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/index.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts (`connect`, `applyAutoVacuumIncremental`, `SQLITE_FILE_REFUSALS`, `releaseRefusedSqliteConnection`, `isSqlite`, `clientSpelling`, `sqliteFilename`), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sqlite-database-file.ts (`SqliteDatabaseFileError`), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the LEVEL axis), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`CATEGORIES`), scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs (`SHAPES`), packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts, .changeset/24837-managed-datasource-sync-refused.md; the changeset .changeset/25019-wasm-unreadable-file-refused.md is judged under ②.

Face: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, line-initial on the PR body and in the changeset; no published schema and no governed path in the committed file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success). Inputs: card #25019's body and all nine comments (the binding ruling 6311031589, route A, member 3; the dev report 6339572437), PR #25200's body, file list and net diff against merge-base `14e7239e7` (6 files, +527/-63), and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Ruling 6311031589, item by item:

1. **`WasmSqliteConnection.open()` refuses a file sql.js cannot read, in every mode, naming the file, with `SQLITE_NOTADB` / `SQLITE_CORRUPT`; nothing renamed, no empty database in its place; `quarantineCorruptFile` retires** — delivered. The `catch` around `new SQL.Database(bytes)` plus `assertReadable` now closes the half-opened handle and throws `unreadableDatabaseFileRefusal(this.filename, err)`: an `Error` carrying `code`, `filename` and `cause`. `open()` reads no mode, so the refusal is unconditional. `quarantineCorruptFile` is deleted; it was `private`, and `index.ts` is untouched, so nothing exported is renamed or replaced. The orphaned-WAL parking moved below the accept, so a refused file keeps its sidecar as well (pinned). Right.
2. **`resolveSqliteDriver` re-throws a wasm file refusal instead of stepping down to the in-memory rung** — delivered, with the two lines the native rung already uses: `closeQuietly(wasmDriver)` then `if (isSqliteFileOpenFailure(err)) throw err`. The predicate is unchanged (`E*`, `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`, `SQLITE_NOTADB`, `SQLITE_CORRUPT`; no message text). `closeQuietly` writes nothing: the connection whose `open()` threw never entered the pool, so `destroyRawConnection` → `close()` → `flush()` never runs on it, and `SqlDriver.connect()`'s own `catch` had already run `releaseRefusedSqliteConnection` (destroy and re-initialise, never throws). Every other wasm failure still reaches the in-memory rung, the `throw` being guarded. Right.
3. **The durability self-heal case becomes a refusal pin** — delivered: it asserts class, code, `filename`, the prescription, `readdirSync(dir)` equal to `['corrupt.db']`, the bytes equal to the junk written, and no "Quarantined" warning. Right.
4. **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, BREAKING** — delivered on the PR body and in the changeset, with the BREAKING banner. The `minor` half is judged in ②.
5. **No option, no knob, no leaving it, no header sniff in the consumer** — delivered: `SqliteWasmDriverConfig` and `sqlite-wasm-driver.ts` are untouched (no option), `sqlite-driver-fallback.ts` reads only `err.code` (no bytes), and `open()` keeps no quarantine branch. Right.

The one-vocabulary claim ("the native driver's class, code and words, with no `driver-sql` edit") holds in the cited code: `SqliteWasmDriver` overrides `isSqlite` to `true` (its class-valued `client` would otherwise spell as `''`), so `SqlDriver.connect()` runs `applyAutoVacuumIncremental`; its `PRAGMA auto_vacuum` is the first acquire, `Client_WasmSqlite.acquireRawConnection` awaits `conn.open()`, knex's pool propagates the create error, and the `catch` maps `code` through `SQLITE_FILE_REFUSALS` into `new SqliteDatabaseFileError(filename, words, e)` — `filename` from `sqliteFilename()` (the declared `connection.filename`), the wasm refusal as `cause`, its message the tail after the colon. That is the operator line the PR body quotes, and both pins assert `name === 'SqliteDatabaseFileError'` through `connect()`. Right.

The code mapping: sql.js throws a bare `Error` carrying SQLite's errstr and no result code, so the producer maps the one text `'file is not a database'` to `SQLITE_NOTADB` and every other read failure (a malformed image, a `quick_check` that does not answer `ok`) to `SQLITE_CORRUPT`; the only downstream reader is `code`. Should a later sql.js re-word that errstr, the code degrades to `SQLITE_CORRUPT`, which the predicate and the table still refuse — a less specific word, never a resolved connect. Right, and in the right place: producer side, one site.

Unchanged behaviour, read in the code and pinned:
- an absent file: the `ENOENT` branch above the hunk is untouched, `new SQL.Database()`; pinned by "an absent file is created" and by the step-down control (native addon cannot load, absent file, still wasm with `NATIVE_SQLITE_WASM_FALLBACK_WARNING`);
- a real database: `bytes` are read before the hunk in both versions; sql.js opens the in-memory image; `quick_check` answers `ok`; the WAL sidecar is parked exactly as before, after the accept instead of before it (the loaded image never read the sidecar); `this.db = candidate`. Pinned at the wasm layer and through `DatasourceConnectionService` in development and production;
- an empty file: a zero-length `Uint8Array` is truthy, sql.js opens it as an empty database; pinned;
- a refused file prints neither step-down line: the wasm warning is emitted only when `wasmOk`; pinned.

Public-surface changes the diff implies: `WasmSqliteConnection.open()` and `SqliteWasmDriver.connect()` reject where they resolved (the narrowing); `resolveSqliteDriver` rejects at the wasm rung for the predicate's codes where it resolved to memory (its second half); `DatasourceConnectionService` reads `failed` where it read `available`. No export is added, removed or re-typed: `UnreadableDatabaseFileCode` and `UnreadableDatabaseFileRefusal` are module-private. The refusal prose carries no tracker number. Right.

Rejection pins assert `code`, `filename`, the message, the directory listing and the file bytes at both layers; a control stands for every "Unchanged" line of the changeset. The ablation (quarantine restored, 6 + 7 red, controls green) is the dev's own reading and was not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

Both packages are published (no `private` field in either manifest), both carry `patch`, and `Metadata-protocol: none` sits beside `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset. `patch` is right.

- The level rule in force on this base is AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 and the LEVEL axis of `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (maintainer ruling A on #25105, filed 2026-10-21, landed as PR #25114 `f2b6cf230`): the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone; a declared `none` grades every entry `patch`; "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". Nothing a metadata author writes moves here: no spec key, no datasource config key (`SqliteWasmDriverConfig` untouched), no default. The kind `none` is honest. `minor` beside `none` is exactly what the gate refuses, and `narrowed` would assert an authorable narrowing that does not exist.
- The seat ruling's item 4 (`minor`) was written at 07:58Z on 2026-10-21, before the maintainer's ruling A was filed (10:11Z) and landed (13:25Z) that same day. A seat ruling under PM discretion yields to the maintainer's rule on the one axis it amends; the ruling's substance (the `(narrowing)` arm, BREAKING, both packages carried) is intact. No regrade owed.
- `Check Changeset` on this head: `success` — the level gate accepted `patch` with `none`, and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` accepted `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a `CATEGORIES` member and the same marker as the precedent `24837-managed-datasource-sync-refused.md`, which has this exact shape (`patch`, narrowing arm, `none`, BREAKING banner).
- The changeset body against the diff: FROM names the retired rename to `FILE.corrupt-TIMESTAMP`, the empty replacement and the wasm rung's bare `catch` — all in the removed lines. TO names `SqliteDatabaseFileError` with both codes and `filename` from `SqliteWasmDriver.connect()`, the same `code` and `filename` from `open()` (correctly not claiming the class there), the WAL left in place, the re-throw at the wasm rung, and other wasm failures still stepping down — all in the added lines. Unchanged names the three controls that are pinned. The fix line matches the message's own prescription. "The native driver already refuses the same files at connect" is true on this base (PR #25006, PR #25080).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6339572437, `open_questions`:

1. **Changeset level.** Answered in ②: `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none` is right under the maintainer's ruling A; the seat ruling's `minor` is superseded on the level only. Not escalated.
2. **A `foreign-vocabulary` row for `SQLITE_NOTADB` / `SQLITE_CORRUPT` in `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts`.** Unneeded for this PR, and wrong as a row. The gate's `SHAPES` derive the assign position only as `assign` (`.code = 'X'`, a quoted literal right after the `=`) and `assignconst` (`.code = CONST`); the ternary `refusal.code = reason === SQLITE_NOTADB_ERRSTR ? 'SQLITE_NOTADB' : 'SQLITE_CORRUPT'` matches neither, so no site is derived — exactly as `SqliteDatabaseFileError`'s own ternary (`this.code = typeof code === 'string' ? code : undefined`) and the `SQLITE_FILE_REFUSALS` map keys derive none in `driver-sql`. The gate reconciles rows against derived sites in both directions ("a table row whose site is gone fails"), so a row for a site the scan does not see would red the gate rather than green it. `Lint · docs & code guards`, the lane that runs `pnpm check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`, is `success` on this head. Whether the gate should learn a ternary at the assign position is a card on the gate's own population (its header already records that position as unclosed), neither this PR's nor a ledger row's; the wasm names share the status the native copies have had since PR #25006. Not required for correctness; no separate card owed by this card.

Dev flags in the PR's acceptance notes:
- knex's `Acquire connection error:` warn with the refusal's stack on each acquire attempt: knex's own logger on a failed pool create, the same for every dialect's refused connection; not a defect of this repo. Noted correctly, nothing to file.
- The development telemetry sibling's catch-all (`packages/cli/src/utils/telemetry-datasource.ts`): named per family note 6305864303 and excluded by the claim. Right.
- #25084: a wasm refusal holds no pooled connection; `releaseRefusedSqliteConnection` still runs on the `catch` and never throws. Right, nothing to add.
- Every non-NOTADB read failure classified `SQLITE_CORRUPT`: judged right in ①.
- "An operating-system failure reading the file (`EACCES`) is not this path and is unchanged": true. By code reading only, NOT MEASURED: wasm `open()` re-throws a non-`ENOENT` `readFile` error raw, `applyAutoVacuumIncremental` has no refusal row for `E*` codes, so the wasm driver's `connect()` logs `Failed to set PRAGMA auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL` and resolves, and an explicit `sqlite-wasm` datasource over a file the process may not read would still read `available`; on the step-down the native rung refuses such a file before wasm sees it. Pre-existing and outside the ruling's five items; handed to the seat to card or dismiss, not a hold on this PR.

Dev `deviations`, each read:
- Branch `claude/project-thread-25g3fn` rather than `claude/issue-25019-*`: the claim 6335885549 names that branch, and "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" is `success`. Fine.
- `main` moved seven commits past the merge at `e39b18e5` and was not merged in: the after-PR merge rule (AGENTS.md §10) says exactly that; the one `driver-sql` commit named is a different region of `sql-driver.ts`; the queue rebuilds on current `main`. Fine.
- Dogfood battery at `e39b18e5`, one commit behind this head: the only later commit, `cda55e654`, names a type alias, and the dev reports the rebuilt `dist/index.mjs` and `dist/index.js` byte-identical by md5. Accepted as pinned by equivalence. Its one red, a 10 s `beforeAll` timeout in `showcase-single-platform-insert-default-organization.dogfood.test.ts`, reproduced on a control with `wasm-connection.ts` at base, so it is the box and not the change; `Dogfood Regression Gate` on this head is `success`; CI's full battery on `main` is the reading of record. The lane seat re-reads this at ACCEPT.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally: `Lint · repo & tooling gates` is `success` on this head.
- No review request written, the attribution line linking the card thread, model-free trailers: outside this review's face.

Check-runs on this head as read 2026-10-22T11:34Z: 27 success, 7 skipped, 6 in_progress — the six `Test Core (n/6)` shards. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` all `success`; every run's `head_sha` is this head. An in_progress shard is a reading, not a pass: the queue's own condition (this record PASS and every check green) is the seat's to re-read before arming; this verdict covers ①②③ only.
